title: Selling and Promotion - Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA - Promotion: Role and Types
subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What is the primary role of promotion in marketing?
options: To transport products from the manufacturer to the retailer.
To inform, persuade, or remind consumers about a business's products or services.
To legally patent a new product idea.
To determine the manufacturing cost of a good.
questions.explain: Promotion encompasses all communication used to inform, persuade, or remind people about a company's offerings or brand.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of 'institutional promotion'?
options: A commercial announcing a buy-one-get-one-free sale on athletic shoes.
A billboard showing a newly released smartphone's camera features.
A company releasing a commercial highlighting its recent donations to clean ocean water initiatives.
An email highlighting a 20% discount on summer apparel.
questions.explain: Institutional promotion focuses on creating a positive image for a company and building goodwill, rather than directly selling a specific product.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which statement best contrasts product promotion with institutional promotion?
options: Product promotion builds brand reputation, while institutional promotion focuses on immediate sales.
Product promotion creates demand for a specific good/service, while institutional promotion creates a favorable image of the business.
Product promotion is free, while institutional promotion is always paid.
Product promotion is only used by B2B companies, while institutional promotion is used by B2C companies.
questions.explain: Product promotion explicitly markets a specific item or service to drive sales. Institutional promotion focuses on public relations and overall corporate image.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: In the concept of promotion, what does the acronym AIDA stand for?
options: Analysis, Information, Demand, Action
Attention, Interest, Desire, Action
Awareness, Interaction, Distribution, Assessment
Action, Intent, Design, Awareness
questions.explain: AIDA is a classic marketing model outlining the stages of a consumer's journey: Attention, Interest, Desire, and Action.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A primary difference between primary product promotion and secondary product promotion is:
options: Primary promotion focuses on an entire class of products, while secondary promotion highlights a specific brand.
Primary promotion is always done online, while secondary promotion is done in print.
Primary promotion focuses on price, while secondary promotion focuses on quality.
Primary promotion is meant for children, and secondary is meant for adults.
questions.explain: Primary promotion aims to stimulate demand for an entire industry or product category (e.g., 'Got Milk?'), whereas secondary (selective) promotion promotes a specific brand.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A 'pull' promotional strategy relies heavily on:
options: Heavy consumer advertising and sales promotions to build demand, encouraging consumers to request the product from retailers.
Offering bulk discounts to wholesalers to push the product onto store shelves.
Salespeople making cold calls to other businesses.
Relying strictly on negative publicity.
questions.explain: A pull strategy is designed to create consumer demand directly through advertising. Consumers then 'pull' the product through the distribution channel by demanding it from retailers.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A business donates 5% of all holiday profits to a local children's hospital and runs an ad highlighting this partnership. What is the business trying to accomplish?
options: Liquidate inventory using a push strategy.
Enhance its corporate image and build goodwill through institutional promotion.
Avoid paying sales tax on retail goods.
Execute a hostile takeover of a competing hospital.
questions.explain: Highlighting charitable partnerships is a textbook example of institutional promotion, designed to build community goodwill and a positive brand image.
